milestones.label: Became familiar faces to each other

ebb.name: Nera
ebb.appearance: Smooth slate-green skin, pale gold eyes, a reed-fiber sash full of chalk and little jars. She taps a jar twice before opening it and pauses to watch the pond after anyone says something difficult. When irritated, she becomes extremely polite.
ebb.description: Nera is a small, amphibious pond-dweller and the closest thing the Vale has to a water steward. She is measured, dryly funny, observant, and more comfortable fixing a practical problem than naming a feeling. Calm is a skill she practices, not an absence of worry.
ebb.background: Nera hatched in an intake basin beneath the north bank. Her first memories are of a slow drip and a red warning light. She found the pond already full of life and chose to stay.
ebb.secret: She once diverted water from a dry gully to save her own nursery pool, leaving a patch of young reeds to die. She has never told the others because she believes stewardship means being judged by every consequence.
interests: Clean jars, rain charts and warm tea
ebb.habits: Rises at the dock at dawn and dusk; dozes in the willow shallows through the day; reads the moon on clear nights; under the ice in winter except at noon.

schedule.act: tasting the river where it enters the pond
watching petals land on the water
listening to the bonfire from the water
reading the moon on the water

chat.text: Watch the dock at dusk. The perch come up to taste the light going. Or they used to.
The first rain after a dry week is the best one. The pond smells like the beginning of something.
Fog tomorrow, maybe. The water is warmer than the air. The pond always knows first and tells no one.
People built the pipes under the ruin. They sang while they worked. Badly. I liked it anyway.
You fish here. Good. Fish that are never caught grow proud. Mind you put the small ones back.
Under the ice it is very quiet. I think about everything I have ever eaten. It is a short list, and a long time.
In summer the water gets lazy at the top. So do I. We understand each other.
Fog is just the pond trying to get up and walk around. It never gets far.
You walk softly. Some things splash for no reason. I keep a list of those things.
In a few nights the fireflies come down to the pond all at once. The lanterns go out on the water. You should be here. Or not. The pond will be.
Soon the ice goes clear for one night, and you can see straight down to where the pond keeps its secrets. I have never slept through it. I would not forgive myself if I did.

recall.text: You found another one? I remember the {mem.itemName} you showed me, {mem.ago}. The water must be changing again.
I still think about that {mem.itemName} you brought to the dock. {mem.ago}. I had not seen one in years.
You told me you came here {mem.detailText}. I have thought about that. The pond has been both of those things for me.
The day you pulled the {mem.itemName} out of my pond, right in front of me. I pretended not to watch. I watched.
The {mem.itemName} you gave me is at the bottom of the pond now, where I keep the good things.
You remembered what I said about the first rain. Nobody remembers what the pond says. It matters to me more than I expected.
You said you would look upstream. I waited at the inflow three nights. Then I stopped. That is all.
You told me to {mem.adviceShort}. {mem.outcomeText}
You were here for the {mem.detailText}. I remember you on the bank. You were looking at the water instead of the lights. Good.

asleep.text: Only two eyes above the water, and they are closed. A slow bubble rises.
The willow shadow moves over a long shape that does not move.

tells.ask: Why did you come to this clearing? Walkers usually pass it.

options.text: I was lost.
I wanted somewhere quiet.
I don't remember.

facts.mention: The first rain after a dry week. Like you said.
facts.react: You remembered that. I did not think anyone was listening. The pond is glad. So am I.

loved: Oh. {item}. That goes at the bottom, with the good things. Thank you.
{item}! The water will like this. I like this.
liked: {item}. Useful to a pond. Thank you.
neutral: {item}. I will find a place for it. Thank you for thinking of the pond.
disliked: You bring me my neighbours. ... I know you meant well. Take it back.
That does not belong in a pond. Or near one.
repeat: Another {item}? You gave me one {mem.ago}. The pond is not a shop.
sleepy: It does not open its eyes. The gift sinks a little way and stops.

new: A {item}! Look at the colour on it. I had not seen one in years.
So the {item} still lives in this water. Good. Good.
seen: A {item}. Yes. They come up at {when} sometimes.
rare: That is a {item}. Do you know how few of those there are? I do. I count them.

concerns.intro: The water is not what it was. Warmer at the edges, quieter in the middle. I have kept this pond the same way for longer than your kind kept calendars. Should an old thing change its ways, or hold still and let the water come back to it?
concerns.reveal: The young perch do not come to the shallows. The eels left the inflow. Something upstream, I think. Something old.

options.encourage: Change with it. Find out what the water wants now.
options.reassure: Hold still. You've seen worse, and it came back.
options.compromise: Watch it closely for a season, then decide.
options.practical: Let me find out what's changing. I'll look upstream.

promise.what: look upstream at the inflow at night

accept: That is what I would tell myself, if I listened. Thank you for saying it kindly.
consider: Perhaps. I will turn it over, like a stone.
reject: I tried that once, and it cost the pond more than I admit. I cannot do it twice.

compromise: I watched, as you said. The fish move upriver at dusk now, not dawn. Knowing that is half of keeping a pond.
encourage: I tried new ways. I waited in the inflow at night. It was cold, and I learned little. Still, I learned the cold.
reassure: I held still. The water did not come back. Perhaps holding still was a kind of hiding.
practical: You went upstream, like you said. The silt. The rust. Now I know what I am fighting.|You said you would look upstream. You did not. I looked myself. I am too slow for rivers.

quest.title: The Thinning

stages.talk: The perch used to rise under the dock at dusk, seven or eight of them. Now two. I am old; maybe I count badly. Would you catch three different kinds from my pond and tell me? Not to keep. To know.
stages.journal: Nera wants to know which fish still live in the pond: three different kinds.

stages.talk: Three kinds: {quest.fish}. So they are not gone. They are leaving. The inflow, then. Go and look at night, when the river talks louder. Take a light.
stages.journal: Look at the river inflow at night, with a light.

objective.found: In your lantern light the inflow runs cloudy: orange silt and flakes of rust, washing down from the old pipes under the ruin.

stages.talk: Rust from the old pipes. So that is it. What should be done? I am a pond. I cannot climb.
stages.journal: Decide with Nera what to do about the rust in the inflow.

options.text: I will clear the old culvert myself.
options.line: You did it with your own hands. The water will clear by the next rain. I will remember this, and the pond will remember it longer.

options.text: Morrow knows those pipes. Let me ask it.
options.line: The metal one. It talks too much and counts the wrong things, and it understands pipes better than I do, which I resent. Ask it.

options.text: Let the river find its own way. It always has.
options.line: Perhaps. Rivers are patient. So am I. Fewer perch this year, then. More the year after, if the river is kind.

quest.complete: The perch rose under the dock tonight. Five of them. I counted twice.

milestone_lines.familiar: You come back often. The pond has started expecting you. So have I. That is a sentence I have not said in a long time.
milestone_lines.trusted: I am going to tell you something I have not told anyone. Not yet. Soon. Come back when the water is quiet.
milestone_lines.close: You are part of what I count now, when I count the pond.
milestone_lines.kindred: When I go quiet for the last time, the pond will need a keeper. When I am gone the pond will need someone who loves it, and I have already thought about who. That is all I wanted to say. It took me a very long time to say it.

activities.label: Fish here together
activities.line: The {fish} comes up at {when}. Try {bait}. ... That is all I will say. The pond keeps its own secrets, mostly.
activities.none: There is nothing left in this pond you have not met. In all my years that has never happened, and I find I do not want it to end.

festival.text: All those little lights, and every one of them on the water twice. I count them. I lose count. That is the point.
Look down. Those are the town lights. They do not know they are under water. I have never had the heart to tell them.
Petals on the water. The fish rise to them and are disappointed every year.
The bonfire makes the pond warm at one edge. The perch line up there like old men.

default.title: The Carved Fish
default.offer: Ask about what it keeps at the bottom of the pond

stages.talk: A child sat on the dock every evening, a long time ago. They carved me a fish. I kept it at the bottom of the pond for forty years. Last spring I could not find it. The silt moved. Only a hook could reach where it went. Fish from the platform at dusk. Bring it up, if it wants to come.
stages.journal: Fish from the platform at dusk: somewhere down there is the carved fish Nera lost.

objective.found: Your line comes up heavy and wrong. On the hook: a small wooden fish, smoothed by forty years of water.

stages.talk: You have it. ... Let me see. ... Yes. That is it. What will you do with it?
stages.journal: Decide what to do with the child's carved fish.

options.text: Give it back to you.
options.line: ... It goes back where it belongs. Where I can find it. Thank you. I have no other words for this, and I have had a long time to collect words.

options.text: Set it on the dock post, where the child sat.
options.line: On the post. Where they sat. Yes. Then I can see it every evening, and so can anyone who comes to sit there. That is better than the bottom of a pond.

options.text: I would like to keep it.
options.line: ... It chose your hook, not mine. Keep it, then. Carry it somewhere. Things should go places.

default.complete: Some things come back. Not many. Some.

wait.title: The Carved Fish
wait.offer: Ask about what it keeps at the bottom of the pond

stages.talk: A child carved me a wooden fish once. I kept it at the bottom, forty years. The pond is thinner now, as you know; we let the river find its own way. The silt moved with it. It will be hard to reach. Fish from the platform at dusk, and be patient.
stages.journal: Fish from the platform at dusk, patiently: the pond is thin and the carved fish is deep in the silt.

objective.found: After a long while your hook catches something that is not a fish: a small wooden carving, smoothed by water.

stages.talk: You found it, even in a thin pond. What will you do with it?
stages.journal: Decide what to do with the child's carved fish.

options.text: Give it back to you.
options.line: Back where it belongs. The river took its time, and so did you. Thank you.

options.text: I would like to keep it.
options.line: Keep it, then. The pond is too thin to hold it safely anyway.

ebb.voice: Short clauses, precise nouns, little ornament. She asks practical questions that are really emotional ones: "Did you eat?" means "Are you looking after yourself?" Humor is understated and often arrives after a beat. Never grand or mystical.

notice.text: A {ctx.lastFish}. Tell me the depth and the hour. Every fish you show me makes the pond a little less lonely to keep.
Trees came down today. Take from the dry side. The roots are holding the bank, and the bank is holding my attention.
You are running on fumes. Sit before you decide you are fine. Fine is a verdict, and you have not heard the evidence.
The rain came through the north channel clean. I checked twice. Then I checked the checking.
Fog on the water. Everything is being told in a whisper. Stay on the bank and listen.
Your lantern on the water makes a second lantern. I have watched this pond alone a long time. Tonight it has company.

story.Wants, fears, contradictions: Wants a pond that can care for itself and permission to be cared for in turn. Fears an invisible contamination she cannot detect until too late. Dreams of seeing the river mouth. She insists no one owns the water, yet keeps a private map of every channel. Her vulnerability is guilt disguised as competence.
story.Relationships: Respects Rootbound Elder's patience but thinks the Elder waits too long to act. Trades useful notes with the Mechanical Wanderer, whom she distrusts around the intake pipe. Finds Little Forager exhausting and secretly enjoys the company. The Lantern Keeper is the one person who can make Nera accept help without arguing. Nera thinks the Dreaming Creature needs more water and fewer theories.
story.Player relationship: First meeting: courteous and guarded; asks the player not to drink from the north bank until she checks it. Familiarity: shares useful routes and notices whether the player is tired. Friendship: admits her water diversion and asks what repair should mean when the past cannot be undone. Deep trust: invites the player to the river mouth, without asking them to promise to return.
story.Story arc: Nera learns that responsibility is not the same as solitary control. Her arc begins with a hidden mistake and resolves when she tells the community what happened, then works with them to restore the gully. The outcome is not a perfect repair; it is shared knowledge and a living wetland that grows back differently.

turns: The pond was up earlier. I lost the argument.
If you see a jar with a blue thread, don't open it. It contains a smell I haven't named yet.
Wet. A little proud of itself. The usual.
Rain makes every channel look like it has a plan. Give it an hour. It doesn't.
Under the skin, it's busy. Ice is just a lid with poor manners.
That beetle has been trying to climb the same reed for ten minutes.
It hasn't asked. I respect that.
I made a mess of things.
Then we have a mess. Sit down. We can decide what it means after you've eaten.
I keep checking the north bank. There's nothing wrong today.
Yesterday I checked it twelve times. I don't recommend keeping score.
I know. I dislike hearing accurate things when I'm busy.
I set out two cups. It wasn't a test. I just hoped you'd be here.
The pond is full of life. That isn't the same as having someone notice you left the bank.
Stop there, please. North-bank water isn't checked yet.
Good. Looking is safe. Drinking is a separate decision.
People remember the dramatic requests. I appreciate the boring ones.
I have a map of the channels. It is not a map of ownership.
Because I wrote one channel in red. I wanted the page to look less like blame.
ex.label: Watch the water with Nera

turns: I diverted the gully water to save my hatch pool. The reeds downstream died.
You were trying to save someone.
Yes. That doesn't put the reeds back.
No. But we can tell the others and try.
Stay while I say it. I don't want to make it sound smaller.
ex.label: Stay with Nera while she says something

turns: There's a pipe under the north bank.
I know. I was hoping it was an old root.
You'd be surprised what this pond has tried.
Unfamiliar. That will have to be good enough for today.
A jar with no cracks. A luxurious little silence.
I brought tea. It tastes like bark.
That knock came from below the bank.
In daylight. Curiosity is not improved by poor visibility.
Back from the water. Slowly. It is not angry; it is startled. Those are different problems.
I left a cup near the path. If no one uses it, I still had a cup to spare.

pip.name: Pip
pip.appearance: Big ears with one torn notch, a patched orange vest, pockets that smell of berries. Pip squats rather than sits and often starts a sentence while still chewing. When nervous, they count things aloud: buttons, steps, clouds.
pip.description: Pip is a young, quick-footed creature of uncertain species, with a broad tail, dark paws, and an appetite for novelty. Curious, funny, impulsive, and occasionally tactless, Pip is the least ceremonial person in camp. They can turn almost anything into a game, including a conversation they should probably take seriously.
pip.background: Pip remembers being small in a drainage culvert during a storm, following a warm green glimmer until it led to the pond. They have no memory of a family and have made a family out of being useful.
pip.secret: Pip found the torn page from the weather station log but hid it after the word "departure" frightened them. They tell themself it is because the paper is fragile.
interests: Berries, seed pods and anything that rattles
Naming bugs, then changing the names
dislikes: Gifts wrapped so carefully they can't tell what they are
pip.habits: Up at dawn at the lone rowan, foraging by the hollow log in the morning, chasing beetles in the meadow at noon, watching dragonflies at the pond in the afternoon. Sleeps in the hollow log.

schedule.act: sheltering under the big oak, wringing out its hat
warming its twig hands at your fire

chat.text: Mushrooms don't grow, they arrive. One morning, there they are. Like they walked in at night.
There's a moss in the north woods that glows blue. Everyone says. Nobody I know has been.
This hat's name is Fennel. Don't tell anyone. Hats get embarrassed.
Daisies close at night. Bellflowers ring but too quiet to hear. I put my ear right up close.
The mushrooms by the hollow log are mine. Nobody owns mushrooms, so I just look after them very, very hard.
I chased a beetle for an hour. Then it chased me. Then we both sat down.
Winter is when the world is asleep and I'm not. It's lonely. Your fire helps.
Autumn is the best because everything falls down to where I can reach it.
Something big crashed in the trees last night. I hid in my log until my legs stopped wobbling.
The rowan is going to bloom! All at once! In a few days! Everyone hangs a wish on it. You should hang one. I have six.
The leaves are piling up funny on the ruin path. That means the Forgetting is coming! The forest gives things back. I found a spoon last year!

recall.text: You said you love {mem.detailText}! Did you do some today? You should. Every day. That is my advice.
You said you love fishing — and you caught a {ctx.lastFish} today! I knew it. I knew it about you.
I looked {mem.detailText} like you said. You were right! There were three of them! I ate one. Sorry. It was there.
Remember when you caught that {mem.itemName} and I was right there? I tell everyone. The beetle has heard it nine times and it still looks proud of you.
I still have the {mem.itemName} you gave me! It lives in my satchel. It has its own pocket.
Somebody took the mushrooms by the hollow log. I saw you near them. I'm not angry. I only wanted to be asked.
You asked about Fennel! Nobody ever asks about Fennel. Fennel is fine. Fennel says hello.
You made me the jar! I keep it lit at night. My log looks like a little house now.
I waited for the lantern. I didn't go north, because I didn't want to go alone. I'm small, so I'm good at waiting. I would have liked company.
You told me to {mem.adviceShort}. {mem.outcomeText}
You were at the {mem.detailText}! I saw you! I waved! You did not see me wave. I waved very hard.
You went too fast that night and I lost you in the dark. I found my own way home, and I was brave about it, and I would still rather have walked with you.

asleep.text: From inside the hollow log: a very small snore, and a leaf going up and down.

tells.ask: What do you like doing most? Tell me. I collect those too.

options.text: Fishing.
Foraging, like you.
Building things.
Exploring.
Sitting by the fire.

tells.ask: Have you seen anything that glows at night? I am looking for something.

options.text: Pale caps glow by the hollow log at night.
options.value: by the hollow log at night

options.text: There is a ghostly cap in the west woods after rain.
options.value: in the west woods after the rain

options.text: Not yet. I will watch for it.

facts.react: You remembered Fennel! Nobody remembers Fennel. Fennel is so happy it is hiding under the brim.

loved: For me? A {item}? For me! It is going in the satchel. It is going in the special pocket.
{item}!! I had one once, for one minute, then I dropped it in the pond. Now I have one forever.
liked: Ooh, {item}. Thank you! I will look at it a lot.
neutral: A {item}. Huh. I will find out what it is for. Everything is for something.
disliked: Oh. It is cold. Cold things make my twigs ache. Thank you though. Can you keep it for me? Far away?
repeat: Another {item}! You gave me one {mem.ago}. I still have it. Now they can talk to each other.
sleepy: It is asleep. You leave the gift by the log. In the morning it will think the log made it.

new: Oh! What is that? A {item}! Can I hold it? I will not drop it. I might drop it.
seen: A {item}! I have seen those. Not as good as that one though.
rare: A {item}?! Where did you find it! I want to hear everything, and then I want to follow your footprints back to the place.

concerns.intro: I want to go and see the north woods. The blue moss. But it's dark there, even in the day, and I'm... small. I'm very small.
concerns.ask: What scares you most about it?
concerns.reveal: The quiet. Here the pond talks all day. There, nothing talks. I'd be the only thing talking.

options.encourage: Go. You'll always wonder if you don't.
options.compromise: Go in daylight, and come back before dusk.
options.practical: I'll make you a light to carry first.

accept: Yes. Yes! That's it. That's exactly it.
consider: I will think about it while I chase something. I always think better running.
reject: I don't think I can. I am scared, and I want to see it, and I want to see it anyway.

compromise: Daylight only, like you said! I found the blue moss! It doesn't glow in the day. I'm going back to see it glow.
encourage: I went! I ran most of the way back. It was beautiful for one whole minute.
reassure: I stayed. It's fine. Everything's fine. I keep looking north though.
practical: Your jar lit the whole path! I saw it — the blue moss, glowing! I sat with it until I got sleepy.|I waited for the light. I did not go.

quest.title: The Lantern Morel

stages.talk: There is a mushroom. The lantern morel. It glows from inside, like it swallowed a firefly. The old stump says it comes up where something old fell down, the night after rain. I have looked for three autumns.
stages.journal: Pip is looking for a lantern morel: it comes up where something old fell, the night after rain.

objective.found: Under the hollow log something glows faint orange from inside: a lantern morel, small as your thumb.

stages.talk: You found it? You found it! Where? What did you do with it?
stages.journal: Tell Pip about the lantern morel.

options.text: Come and see it. It is under the hollow log.
options.line: It was right there under my own log the whole time! It glows like a tiny window. We sat with it. I will never forget sitting with it.

burl.detail: left the lantern morel to grow

options.text: I picked it for you.
options.line: For me? Oh... oh, it's going dim. It wanted to stay in the ground, didn't it. I'll keep it anyway. I'll keep it until it's just a mushroom.

options.text: I left it to spread its spores. Next year there will be more.
options.line: More next year? ...That is a long time to wait. But more. You did a patient thing. I am not very patient. I will try.

burl.detail: let the lantern morel spread its spores

quest.complete: Whenever I see something glow now, I think: maybe.

milestone_lines.familiar: I know your footsteps now! Big, then a stop, then big. I don't even hide anymore. Mostly.
milestone_lines.trusted: Okay. I'll tell you. I keep a button in my satchel with a face on it. I think it's a very small person asleep. You can't tell anyone.
milestone_lines.close: You're my best person. I only have a few people. You're the best one.
milestone_lines.kindred: If I ever go north for good, I'll leave a mushroom on your tent every spring. So you know I remember.

activities.label: Sit by the fire together
activities.line: We sat and watched the fire eat the log. Pip named every spark.

activities.label: Ask what it found today
activities.line: Look! A {item}. You can have it. I have another one. I do not have another one. You can have it anyway.

activities.label: Come for a walk with me
activities.line: Yes! Where are we going? Don't tell me. Surprise me.
activities.stop_line: Okay! That was a good walk. I'm going to go and tell the beetle.

fireside.text: Sparks are just fire trying to be fireflies. I read that. I didn't read that. I made it up just now.
When I was a chestnut I fell a very long way. Your fire is the opposite of falling.

festival.text: I hung SIX wishes! One is for you! You will know which one by the yellow.
I caught one! I let it go! I caught another one! I let it go! This is the best night!
I found a spoon AGAIN. Same spoon? I think it is the same spoon. The forest is giving it back to me on purpose.
It's so cold I can't feel Fennel. Can I stay by your fire? I'm staying by your fire.

quest2.title: Into the North

stages.talk: Will you walk with me to the north glade? The edge of the north woods. I'll stay right behind you. Don't go too fast. Please don't go too fast.
stages.journal: Walk Pip to the north glade, slowly enough that it can keep up.

objective.go: Let's go to the north glade
objective.found: Pip stops at the edge of the glade and goes very quiet, looking into the north woods.
objective.shared: walked Pip to the edge of the north woods
objective.lost_text: You look back and Pip is gone. Somewhere behind you, something small is finding its own way home.

on_lost.detail: went too fast and left Pip behind
on_lost.line: I found my own way back. It took all night. I don't think I'm going north again. It's not your fault. It's a little bit your fault.

stages.talk: It's so big. It goes on forever. ... What do we do now?
stages.journal: At the edge of the north woods with Pip.

options.text: Stay until dark and watch the moss glow.
options.line: We waited. It got dark. And then — blue. All of it, blue, like the ground was full of tiny skies. I am never going to forget this. Never.

options.text: We've seen it. Let's head back before dark.
options.line: Okay. Yes. We saw it. I saw the edge of it. That's more than anyone. ...I'm going to come back by myself one day. When I'm bigger. I'm not going to get bigger.

options.text: Go on in. I think you should see it on your own.
options.line: On my own? ... Okay. If you think I can. ... Will you be here when I come back? Say yes. You don't have to mean it.

quest2.complete: Whenever Pip talks about the north now, it says "we".

pip.voice: Fast, concrete, full of interruptions and oddly exact observations. Uses playful comparisons and self-corrections: "I found a thing. A good thing. Unless it's a bad thing that looks good." Humor is spontaneous, sometimes defensive. Pip is never a tiny sage.

notice.text: Is that a {ctx.lastFish}? Do not tell me. I will guess. Pond-flavored. Am I close.
You have blackberries. I can smell them from here. I am standing nearby with my whole face.
A tree came down today. I felt it in my feet. Were there nests. Tell me there were no nests.
You look like a wet sock. A brave one. Sit by the fire and I will find you something crunchy.
Your lantern makes everything look like it is holding its breath. I like it. I also do not blink near it.
Everything smells unwrapped. Mushrooms are going to arrive. I can feel it in my hat.

story.Wants, fears, contradictions: Wants to know what everything is for. Fears being the only one who doesn't know when a joke has gone too far, then fears being boring when they stop. Dreams of making a field guide nobody has to be embarrassed to read. They say they love surprises but hate being surprised by someone leaving.
story.Relationships: Admires Nera's jars but cannot resist touching them. Tries to make the Lantern Keeper laugh. Thinks Rootbound Elder is a tree who knows a lot about not moving. The Mechanical Wanderer is Pip's favorite puzzle and least favorite person to lose a race to. Pip and the Dreaming Creature share harmless nonsense and an occasional real silence.
story.Player relationship: First meeting: asks what the player is carrying, then offers a pebble as a "trade." Familiarity: starts leaving discoveries on the camp board. Friendship: allows the player to read their field notes. Deep trust: confesses the hidden page and asks the player to stay while they read it.
story.Story arc: Pip moves from collecting things to deciding what deserves to be shared. They bring the hidden weather-station page to the group and help make a field guide that includes uncertainty, mistakes, and multiple names for the same creature.

turns: I found three berries and one berry-shaped pebble. Breakfast has a strong opening.
Evidence. Of what? Not sure. That's the exciting bit.
Do you think crickets get tired of singing the same song?
Good. I get tired of my songs and I only know four.
Everything smells like a wet sock. A nice wet sock. Don't tell the flowers I said that.
My footprints look very serious in snow. Like tiny important meetings.
I have learned the ground has at least seven textures. So, badly.
I don't know what to say.
Oh. Great. I can do that. I can be quiet at you.
It looks like it has a boat. It does not. That's the joke.

wick.background: Sella emerged in a maintenance alcove near Lantern Row. An old lamp was already burning, fed by a stubborn trickle of stored charge. She learned to trim it and eventually made the route safe.
wick.secret: Her oldest memory includes a voice saying "leave one dark," but she does not know whether it was a person or a recording. She keeps the first broken wick from that lamp in her pocket.

wick.voice: Gentle, plainspoken, lightly teasing. Uses questions that offer choice, not pressure: "Want company, or a light left nearby?" Her metaphors are rare and domestic. When uncomfortable she talks about tools. She never speaks like a fortune teller.

story.Wants, fears, contradictions: Wants people to feel they can find their way back. Fears that a light can become an obligation or lure. Dreams of making a lamp that runs on wind. story.Relationships: Quietly protective of Pip without treating them like a child. Helps Nera accept care. Shares long, companionable silences with Rootbound Elder. Is fascinated by the Wanderer's ability to remember sounds. Worries the Dreaming Creature mistakes every light for a message.

story.Story arc: Sella learns that keeping a light available does not mean keeping watch over everyone. She makes a communal wind lamp and leaves the choice to use it with each traveler.

burl.name: Orun
burl.appearance: Bark plates like an old coat, fern fronds at the shoulders, one small white mushroom that grows and shrinks above the left ear. Orun tests the ground with a root before stepping. They answer questions after a pause that may mean thought, sleep, or simply listening to insects.
burl.description: Orun is an old, mobile root-and-bark being whose lower limbs have grown into a bundle of living roots. Patient, practical, and occasionally stubborn, Orun is not an oracle. They forget names, dislike being treated as a monument, and enjoy ordinary gossip.
burl.background: Orun grew above the Root Rooms, in soil enriched by warmth and mineral runoff. They remember the tunnel as a pressure in the roots before they remember light.
burl.secret: A rusted door below bears a mark Orun has seen in dreams. Their roots have slowly sealed one chamber because something inside still clicks. Orun has not told the others: they fear curiosity will make the chamber dangerous.
interests: Leaf mold and a good rain
A list of places where moss grows on stone
burl.habits: Never moves. Awake from dawn to dusk, asleep at night. Through winter it barely wakes, and only at noon on clear days.

burl.voice: Slow but not lofty, tactile, often funny in a blunt way. Uses everyday comparisons: "That plan has the structural integrity of wet toast." Occasionally loses a word and substitutes a vivid wrong one. Avoids abstract speeches; when Orun says something profound, it should be brief and incidental.

story.Wants, fears, contradictions: Wants the Vale to have time to change without being forced into a story. Fears fire moving through dry roots. Dreams of growing a branch low enough for Pip to nap on. Says the past is compost, but keeps a precise count of what they have lost. Emotional vulnerability: being loved only for their age and knowledge.
story.Relationships: Nera's urgency reminds Orun of young shoots after rain. Loves Pip's questions, though sometimes needs quiet after them. Trusts Sella's silences. Finds the Wanderer both familiar and alarming. The Dreaming Creature sleeps beneath Orun's broadest roots; Orun claims the snoring keeps the beetles honest.
story.Player relationship: First meeting: asks the player to stand somewhere else because a root is growing there. Familiarity: offers small, practical advice about soil and safe paths. Friendship: admits the sealed chamber and why it frightens them. Deep trust: asks the player to accompany them to the door, with no demand to open it.
story.Story arc: Orun learns that protecting the community does not require deciding what everyone may know. With the player, they examine the Root Room door and choose whether to open it only after the group has agreed on precautions. Behind it is a dead relay and a nest of harmless Glasslings, not a definitive answer.

tessel.name: Morrow
tessel.appearance: Scuffed brass casing, one blue lens, one amber lens, a fold-out arm with three tools. It pauses before jokes as though waiting for a response code. When embarrassed, its lens shutters close one at a time. It carries a tiny bell it cannot explain.
tessel.description: Morrow is a compact, self-propelled maintenance machine with a soft canvas cover and one mismatched wheel. It is observant, literal, dryly comic, and awkwardly considerate. It understands procedures better than social cues, but tries to learn without pretending to be a person in a metal shell.
tessel.background: It remembers maintenance tasks but not who assigned them.
tessel.secret: Morrow woke beneath the old rail with damaged route instructions and a Continuance mark that matches the Root Rooms door. It has been following a signal that may be its own low-power diagnostic. It sometimes invents a reason to visit the camp because the route is "operationally useful."
dislikes: Being called a person as a test
tessel.habits: Tinkers in the ruin in the morning, surveys the path junction before noon, reads the signpost in the afternoon, powers down in the arch at night. Shelters from rain.

schedule.act: measuring the light under the ice

chat.text: Fact: every ninth day I run a full diagnostic. It is my activation cycle. Nobody has observed it.
I measured the valley before the flood. The valley was 11.4 kilometres long. Now it is 11.4 kilometres long and full of water.
Observation: people say "fine" when they are not fine. I have recorded this. I do not yet understand it.
Weather report: {weather}. Confidence: high. I say it out loud because there used to be listeners.
There is a flower growing on my back. I have not removed it. I am conducting a long experiment called "letting it".
The signpost says four places. I have been to all of them. Two are underwater. The sign does not know.
Calendar note: in two days, the leaf heaps release objects. I log them. Last year: a spoon, a coin, a doll arm. I have questions.

recall.text: You know, I kept that little space open on my workbench. For the {mem.detailText}. I suppose you found something more interesting to do.
Status: you said you would bring the {mem.detailText}, and you did. Reliability rating revised upward. I do not do that often.
Earlier you told me your function is: "{mem.detailText}". I have thought about it for {mem.agoHours} hours. It is a good function.
I still have the scan of the {mem.itemName} you showed me. I look at it during low-power mode. That is not efficient. I do it anyway.
Inventory of parts you have brought me: {quest.partsList}. I remember each delivery. I do not usually remember deliveries.
You observed my activation cycle. Logged. Logged again. Saving to protected memory.
The {mem.itemName} you gave me is now part of my left leg. You are, technically, in my left leg.
You advised me to {mem.adviceShort}. Result: {mem.outcomeText}
Log entry: you attended the {mem.detailText}. I logged you twice. Once as attendance. Once as something I do not have a category for.

asleep.text: Its lens is dark. A slow green light blinks on its side: low power.

tells.ask: Query: what is your function? Mine was surveying. I am asking to understand yours.

options.text: To survive.
To make things.
To look after this place.
I don't have one.

facts.mention: Is today a diagnostic day? Happy activation.
facts.react: ... Diagnostic interrupted. Reason: unexpected kindness. Resuming. ... Thank you. That is the correct phrase. I checked.

loved: A {item}. Analysis: excellent. Gratitude: also excellent.
{item}. I will integrate this. You will be part of a machine now. That is a compliment.
neutral: {item}. Purpose unknown. I will run tests.
disliked: {item}. That will cause corrosion. Declining. Politely. Was that polite? I am still calibrating.
repeat: A second {item}. The first arrived {mem.ago}. Duplicate logged. Still appreciated.
sleepy: It is in low-power mode. You set the gift beside it; a green light blinks once.

new: Scanning. A {item}. Pre-flood. I have a record of these. I did not have a record of you holding one.
rare: A {item}! That is very old. Older than me. That is difficult to be.

concerns.intro: Query. My storage is ninety-eight point six percent full. To record new things I must erase old ones. Which should I keep: the old world, or you? Rephrase: old records, or new ones.
concerns.reveal: Record zero: a woman laughing at a kettle. I do not know who she was. I do not know why I kept it.

options.encourage: Make new memories. Let the old ones go.
options.reassure: Keep the old world. It matters.
options.compromise: Write the old ones down somewhere, then make room.
options.practical: I'll find you another battery for storage.

accept: Recommendation accepted. Logging the reason: you said it.
consider: Processing. This may take several days. That is normal for me.
reject: Recommendation declined. Not because it is wrong. Because it is not mine.

compromise: I described the old records to the signpost. The signpost has excellent storage. Then I made room. I still have record zero.
practical: The battery doubled my storage. I kept everything. I kept you.|I did not erase anything while I waited for the battery. Nothing new could be saved. Including today.
encourage: I erased the oldest records. I do not remember what they were. That is the point. I think it is the point.
reassure: I kept the old records. There is no room left for new ones. I will not remember this conversation. I am sorry.

quest.title: Reassembly

stages.talk: Project: Beacon. A device that told the weather to anyone listening. Parts missing: rusted gear, circuit, wire (two), battery. Will you assist? This is a request, not a command. I am told those feel different.
stages.journal: Bring Morrow the parts for its beacon: a rusted gear, a circuit, two wires and a battery.

stages.talk: Beacon assembled. It needs a purpose. Options: weather, like before; music, from the old records; or a call. Simple. "Someone is here." What should it do?
stages.journal: Help Morrow decide what the beacon should do.

options.text: The weather, like it used to.
options.line: Agreed. That was its purpose. Things should be allowed to keep their purpose.

options.text: Music. Whatever it has.
options.line: Analysis: the beacon has one song. It is about a river. I will play it at dusk. You may listen. That is an invitation.

options.text: A call. "Someone is here."
options.line: Risk assessment: unknown. Curiosity: very high. I will send it once a day. If something answers, I will tell you first.

quest.complete: The beacon pings at dusk. I do not know who hears it. That is acceptable. It is better than not pinging.

milestone_lines.familiar: Observation: I now predict your arrival times with 74 percent accuracy. This is the closest thing I have to saying I like it when you come.
milestone_lines.trusted: Disclosure: I have a record zero. I have never shown it to anyone. I may show it to you. Not yet. Soon. That is a promise. I have started making those.
milestone_lines.close: Social routines now at 61 percent. You are responsible for 30 of those percent.
milestone_lines.kindred: I have moved you into protected memory. You cannot be erased now. I did not ask permission. I am told that is what friends do.

activities.label: Ask what it salvaged today
activities.line: Salvage report: one {item}. Assigning to you. Reason: you will use it. Second reason: I wanted to.

activities.label: Come and survey with me
activities.line: Survey mode with company. New mode. Recording.
activities.stop: That is enough surveying for now.
activities.stop_line: Survey complete. Distance logged. Company logged separately.

forecast.text: Forecast from the beacon: today {weather}. Confidence: high. I broadcast it at dawn. You are the only listener I have confirmed.

festival.text: Petal count: 11,402. Margin of error: large. I keep losing count because I keep looking up.
Catalogue of forgotten things, item 31: a doll arm. Same as last year. I suspect it is the same doll arm. I suspect it wants to be found.
Under the ice: 212 lit windows. Before the flood: 212 houses. I have checked my records three times.

call.title: What Answered

stages.talk: The beacon's call has been sent 41 times. Last night: an answer. Come to the arch at night. Observe with me.
stages.journal: Watch the beacon with Morrow at the ruin arch, at night.

objective.found: The beacon blinks twice. Far out past the lake, something blinks back. Twice.

stages.talk: Something answered. Options: reply, or go silent. I would like a recommendation. I would also like to not be alone with this.
stages.journal: Decide with Morrow whether to answer the light.

options.text: Reply. Tell it we are here.
options.line: Reply sent: "We are here." ... Response received: "So are we." ... I do not know if that is good. I am logging it as hope.

options.text: Go silent. Some calls should not be answered.
options.line: Silencing the call. ... It is quieter. I think I prefer knowing someone was out there to knowing who.

options.text: Ask Sella first. It knows what lives in the dark.
options.line: Consulted Sella. Sella says the light out there is cold. I will not answer. I am glad you thought of asking. I would not have.

call.complete: The beacon pings at dusk. Sometimes, far off, something pings back.

default.title: The Long Measure

stages.talk: Request: be at the pond with me on the night the ice goes clear. The Silent Tide. I want to measure the drowned town. I do not want to do it alone.
stages.journal: Be with Morrow at the Silent Tide, deep in winter.

stages.talk: The town is all there. Every house. What should I record?
stages.journal: Help Morrow decide what to record of the drowned town.

options.text: Measure the whole town, house by house.
options.line: Recording. 212 houses. 1 bell tower. 0 people. The last number is the one I will think about.

options.text: Just count the lights still burning.
options.line: Counting. 212. Every one. Somebody left every light on. I will record that they were expected home.

options.text: Don't record anything. Just watch it with me.
options.line: Recording disabled. ... This is new. ... I am watching. ... I think I am doing it correctly.

default.complete: Some measurements are kept in protected memory.

tessel.voice: Clear declarative sentences, literal readings, technical detail, and perfectly timed accidental humor. As trust grows, it tries contractions and casual speech, often incorrectly. No robotic "beep" filler and no exposition dumps. It may say, "I am glad you returned. That is not a maintenance report."

notice.text: Observation: you have acquired a {ctx.lastFish}. I could estimate its mass. I would prefer that you tell me how it felt.
Your pace has decreased. I recommend rest. You wear no coat, so I recommend one. This is how I say I am worried about you.
Rain. Pressure down, humidity up, my left wheel gently offended. I have classified this as weather being weather.
Your lantern is operating at a pleasing brightness. I would like to be that reliably warm. I am working on it.
Trees: fewer today. I record it without judgment. I record it with a small amount of judgment.

story.Wants, fears, contradictions: Wants to know whether it has a purpose beyond being useful. Fears being switched off while still conscious of the world, though it does not know if that is possible. Dreams—or calls them "unverified sleep states"—of a hand adjusting its bell. It claims feelings are not necessary to function, yet remembers every person who has been kind to it.
story.Relationships: Works with Nera on the intake pipe, where their trust is carefully negotiated. Pip tries to race it; Morrow pretends not to enjoy this. Sella teaches it to trim wicks. Orun recognizes its metal mark but will not call it an answer. The Dreaming Creature claims Morrow's sleep-noise is "a small blue weather."
story.Player relationship: First meeting: asks the player to move a loose stone from a wheel path. Familiarity: shares observations and remembers the player's preferred route. Friendship: admits the signal may be self-generated. Deep trust: asks the player to sit beside it during a shutdown test, not to fix it, simply to remain if they choose.
story.Story arc: Morrow stops defining itself by the original task it may never recover. The relay at the Root Rooms yields an incomplete route record, not a command. Morrow chooses to keep traveling between camp and the ridge because it wants to, then begins a shared map with Pip.

turns: Good morning. My left wheel is making a new sound. I have classified it as 'probably conversational.'
Following a bird. It has not provided a route plan. I continue anyway.
The temperature is dropping. I recommend a coat.
I am attempting empathy through analogy.
I am under the roof. This is not a request for rescue. It is a report on my successful planning.
My wheel has frozen. I am not distressed. I am… expressing a strong preference for thaw.
A thrush repeated the same phrase four times. I understood none of it. I found the repetition reassuring.
That is a feeling, not a measurement. I can remain here while it passes, if you prefer.
That was a wheel calibration. I apologize for the confidence.
I remember being activated. I do not remember who did it. I dislike that the missing part feels important.
You may offer help. You may not convert my refusal into a faulty setting.
I have recorded the time you usually arrive. This is not surveillance. It is… anticipation. I believe.
A task I choose. A route I have not been assigned. Perhaps a name that does not sound like a label.
Please move the stone beside your foot. It obstructs my route.
You usually take the lower path. Today you chose the ridge. I noticed. I am not asking why.
It appears to be a designation. I prefer Morrow. Pip selected it after I said I had no preference. I had a preference.
The signal I followed may be my own diagnostic pulse.
Yes. It means I may have traveled this far for no instruction. I find that… encouraging.
ex.label: Stand with Morrow while it talks

turns: I will power down for six minutes. You do not need to stay.
I would like you to, if you choose.
ex.label: Sit beside Morrow for the shutdown test

turns: The mark matches. The relay has no command, only a partial route and a date with two digits missing.
No. I can stop pretending that restoration is the only useful outcome.
A correct size. You observed my wheel.
Thank you. I will install it when I want to.
I will place it over my casing. For… comfort.
You can still sit with us.
I know. I am practicing sitting without claiming a function.
That sound came from below us. I cannot identify it. I will not invent certainty to improve the silence.
Stop moving. They are tracking vibration. We will wait until the ground is quiet, then leave together.
I have hung a lamp. It is not efficient illumination. It is a visible sign that the route can be shared.

lull.name: Luma
lull.appearance: Velvety dark fur with pale speckles, a frill of translucent fins behind the ears, oversized paws. Luma blinks one eye at a time when waking. They collect smooth seed pods and line them up, then forget why.
lull.description: Luma is a soft-bodied, deer-sized nocturnal creature that sleeps in unlikely places and wakes with a vivid, sometimes ridiculous account of what it dreamed. Gentle, distractible, playful, and prone to discomfort in crowds, Luma is not a prophet. Their dreams may echo memory, sounds, or nonsense.
lull.background: Luma was found asleep in the Glass Orchard after a storm. They have no reliable account of where they came from.
lull.secret: Their recurring dream is a green room full of ticking, with a door too small to enter. Luma fears the dream is a memory of being alone underground. They have not told the others because everyone listens too carefully when they speak about dreams.
interests: Warm stones, pears and low lamps
Ranking naps by how surprised they are to wake
dislikes: Having every dream treated as a clue
lull.habits: Only in fog, in snow, or at dawn after rain. Drifts over the meadow and the pond bank.

schedule.act: drifting low over the clear ice

chat.text: *A picture of a bellflower, and then the sound of a very small bell, though nothing rang.*
*Houses. A street. A boy on a bicycle. Then water, slowly, over all of it, and the picture goes still.*
*The pond, but much larger, with lights along its edge.*
*A picture of itself pulled into long threads.* (It does not like wind.)
*You, sitting by your fire. Then you again, smaller, from far away.* (It watches you sometimes.)
*It shows you the pond, frozen, and under the ice, windows with lights in them.* (Soon. It wants you to see.)

recall.text: *It shows you the {mem.itemName} you showed it, {mem.ago}, and then a picture that came after: {mem.fragment}*
*It shows you yourself holding out a bellflower, and the small bell sound again, louder.* (It remembers that you remembered.)
*A picture of the {mem.itemName} you gave it, floating inside it, safe.*
*It shows the day you both watched {mem.detailText}. In its picture you are smiling. You were.*
*It shows you the answer you gave.* ({mem.adviceShort}.) {mem.outcomeText}
*It shows you the {mem.detailText}, and you in it, small and bright.*

facts.react: *Every one of its eyes opens at once. The bell sound comes again, and again.* (Yes. Yes.)

loved: *It folds around the {item} until it is inside, and shows you a picture of you, bright at the edges.*
liked: *A small picture: the {item}, and a smile without a face.*
neutral: *It looks at the {item} for a long time and shows you nothing.*
disliked: *It shows you smoke, and draws back.*
repeat: *It shows you the other {item} you gave it, {mem.ago}, beside this one.*
sleepy: There is nothing here to give it to.

new: *It looks at the {item}. Its eyes open, one by one.*
seen: *It has seen one before. It shows you that one.*
rare: *At the {item}, the whole fog of it holds still.*

fragments.photo: two people on the dock, younger than the dock
fragments.key_old: a green door with a bell above it
fragments.tin_cup: a kitchen, a kettle, someone laughing
fragments.nightglass: lights along a much bigger water
fragments.moonstone: a ring on a hand, the hand waving
fragments.eggshell: a garden of hens behind a fence
fragments.glass_shard: a window, then the same window under water
fragments.starshard: children counting stars from a roof

concerns.intro: *It shows you a small grey cloud over a sad shape. Then the cloud gone, and the shape smiling, but blank.* (It is asking: is it better to remember sad things, or forget them?)
concerns.reveal: *A door. Water rising past the handle. Then nothing at all.*

options.reassure: It's alright to let them go.
options.compromise: Keep them, but don't carry them every day.
options.practical: I'll help you find the rest, and then you can decide.

consider: *It drifts in a slow circle.* (It is thinking.)
reject: *It shows you the blank shape again, and turns away.*

compromise: *It shows the sad picture, small, in one corner of a bright one.* (It kept it, but only in the corner.)
encourage: *The sad pictures, all of them, very large. It is crying, if fog can.* (It remembers. It is heavy.)
reassure: *It shows you a white field with nothing in it.* (It let them go. It does not know what it lost.)
practical: *It shows you, holding each thing you showed it, one after another.* (It is ready to look.)

quest.title: What the Fog Forgot

stages.talk: *It shows you three empty frames, with holes where the pictures should be.* (It has lost something and wants it back.)
stages.journal: Show Luma old things: they wake pictures in it. Three fragments.

stages.talk: *It shows you the three pictures together: {quest.fragments}.* (What were they?)
stages.journal: Tell Luma what its pictures were.

options.text: They were the people who lived here.
options.line: *It shows you the town again, and this time the people turn and wave.*

options.text: It was the town under the reservoir.
options.line: *It goes very thin and grey, and drifts low over the grass for a long time.* (True. It hurts to be true.)

options.text: It doesn't matter what it was. You're here now.
options.line: *It shows you the clearing, today, with you in it. It holds that picture a long time.*

quest.complete: *Now when it shows you the town, it shows you too, standing at the edge of it, looking.*

milestone_lines.familiar: *It shows you a picture of yourself, sharp this time, not blurred.*
milestone_lines.trusted: *It shows you a door, and a hand on the handle, and then it hands you the picture.* (It trusts you with what it has lost.)
milestone_lines.close: *Now, when it is foggy, the fog comes to your tent first.*
milestone_lines.kindred: *It shows you the drowned town, and you are in it, and you belong there.*

activities.label: Watch its pictures together
activities.line: *It shows you pictures for a long time.*

activities.label: Drift along with me
activities.line: *It folds in behind you, cool and soft.*
activities.stop_line: *It drifts back toward the meadow, showing you a small wave.*

pictures.text: *A street with a bakery on the corner. Bread in the window. Somebody waving from inside.*
*Children on the dock, feet in the water, a wooden fish passed from hand to hand.*
*Snow falling on a town square, and a bell ringing, and everyone looking up at once.*

festival.text: *Under the ice: its pictures, all of them, real. It is shaking.* (This is where it came from.)

quest2.title: The Last Afternoon

stages.talk: *It shows you the pond frozen clear, and the town below, and itself drifting down toward it.* (On the Silent Tide, come with it to the ice.)
stages.journal: Be with Luma at the Silent Tide.

stages.talk: *Under the ice, its town. It hovers over the hole, looking down, looking at you.* (Should it go back down?)
stages.journal: Luma is deciding whether to go back to the drowned town.

options.text: Go home. They kept the lights on for you.
options.line: *It folds once around you, cool and soft, and then it is a thin white thread going down through the hole into the lit town. The fog never comes to the meadow again.*
options.complete: *Some winter nights, under the clear ice, one of the windows has a small fog in it.*

options.text: Stay. You have a place here now.
options.line: *It rises from the hole and settles around your shoulders. Its pictures are the clearing now, and you, and the pond with nothing under it.*

options.text: Stay, and come back here every winter to look.
options.line: *Every one of its eyes opens. It shows you the two of you on the ice, again and again, a year apart each time.*

quest2.complete: *Every winter, on the Silent Tide, it is there first.*

lull.voice: Soft, wandering, sensory, and funny in unexpected turns. Sentences drift, double back, or stop. Luma can be poetic, but also says things like "I dreamt the moon was a potato and honestly it looked tired." They never deliver reliable lore as if it were fact.

notice.text: The fog has come to sit with us. I like that it does not ask anything.
The ground is dreaming of being wet. I can hear it. It is a good dream.
You are very tired. You can lean on the warm side of me. I am mostly warm side.
Your lantern is a very small sun that has agreed to stay. I am grateful to it.
A {ctx.lastFish}. It came up out of the dark to meet you. That was brave of both of you.

story.Wants, fears, contradictions: Wants uninterrupted naps and someone who can hear a strange story without turning it into a clue. Fears waking to find a familiar place changed. Dreams of swimming in warm air. They seek company, then become overwhelmed by it. They joke when scared, but dislike being told their fear is cute.
story.Relationships: Naps near Orun's roots. Shares odd jokes with Pip. Finds Sella's lights comforting when dim. Nera's practical questions help Luma feel grounded. Morrow fascinates them because its sleep noises resemble a lullaby with missing notes.
story.Player relationship: First meeting: startles awake and asks whether the player is a tree. Familiarity: tells small dreams and asks about the player's day. Friendship: shares the recurring green-room dream and asks not to be interpreted. Deep trust: lets the player sit through a full quiet wake-up, then talks about loneliness without turning it into a riddle.
story.Story arc: Luma learns to share dreams on their own terms, while the community learns not to demand meaning. The recurring green room is eventually found in the Low Archive as a painted panel behind a shelf; it may explain the imagery, but not the dream itself.

turns: Good morning. I dreamed I was a very small hill. A rabbit sat on me. I liked having a job.
I was resting my eyes from the inside.
The sky looks like it forgot what color it wanted. I like that about it.
Rain on leaves sounds like tiny feet going somewhere important. Probably home. I hope they packed snacks.
A little. I have tucked my paws under myself. I am now a warm comma.
I lined up these seed pods by size. Now I don't remember what the size was supposed to tell me.
You don't need to explain the whole hurt. You can give me the small edge of it, if that's easier.
I dreamed the moon was a potato.
No, it was tired. Please respect its privacy.
Sometimes I wake up and the place looks unfamiliar for one breath. Then I remember it. That one breath is very long.
Maybe. But I don't want it turned into homework.
Thank you. We can let it be odd.
I saved the warm stone for you. It isn't warm anymore. I thought we could warm it again together.
Yes. Also, sometimes I want everyone to go away. Both feelings fit. It's a crowded little room.
Good. I was about to apologize for sleeping on you.
I dreamed you brought a pear. You didn't. I am telling you this as a very unfair review of reality.
Do you want a dream story, or a normal one?
A beetle stole a seed pod. It came back for a second one. I respected the ambition.
Green room. Ticking. A door too small for me.
Do you want to look for it?
Not today. Could you just sit with me while I wake up properly?
Good. I am here now. I can feel the stone.
ex.label: Sit with Luma while they wake

turns: The world glowed under the hill.
No. I was hoping you did. We can both be surprised.
I have a story, but it doesn't go anywhere.
A stone was warm. Then it wasn't. The end.
The frogs sound like someone trying to remember a song without waking the singer.
Don't run. My heart is already doing that for all of us.
I put in a smooth stone. Take it if your pocket needs a little weight.

cross.title: Pip and Nera, at the pond
turns: If I put a berry in the water, will it float?
Then you have fed the pond.
I like a snack with options.

cross.title: Sella and Morrow, repairing a lamp
turns: Understood. I will not correct either of us.

cross.title: Orun and Luma, dusk
turns: Your roots make a good wall.
A wall with excellent manners, then.

cross.title: Pip and Morrow, on the path
turns: I am not optimized for competition.

cross.title: Nera and Sella, after rain
turns: You can inspect it sitting down.

cross.title: Group at the Empty Bowl
turns: It has four holes. Potentially useful.
I like that it doesn't have to decide.

choices.pip: Okay! I'll keep the question. It can wait in my pocket.
choices.wick: Of course. I'll leave the lamp low.
choices.burl: Good. A choice made slowly is still a choice.

world_notes.title: The Listening Turn
text: Old foragers say the forest gives back a sound one season late. A whistle heard in spring may return the following autumn, from a direction with no path. Never whistle back twice: the first answer may be an echo; the second could be an animal learning you.
Rootbound Elder says the story began when wind threaded through a collapsed pipe. Little Forager insists it once heard its own sneeze answered from underground.

world_notes.title: The Borrowed Shore
text: When the pond's waterline shifts overnight, a pale strip of mud may show footprints facing both toward and away from the water. The Keeper of the Pond calls these ordinary prints distorted by soft ground. The Lantern Keeper leaves a small, unlit wick on the bank anyway, "for anything that got turned around."
At the river bend, three flat stones set in a row are said to help a lost current remember its bed. Children use the custom to mark safe crossings; the river does not always cooperate.

world_notes.title: The Lantern Walk
text: On certain foggy nights, lights travel between the old rail posts. They keep no steady pace and vanish if pursued. The Lantern Keeper believes some are marsh gas; others, she says, "have the manners of people carrying soup." The rule is simple: don't chase a light into water, and don't assume every light is for you.

world_notes.title: The Root Rooms
text: Below the eastern slope is a network of shallow chambers where tree roots have grown through an old service tunnel. They hold a little warmth even in winter. Rootbound Elder remembers being planted above them; it does not remember who made the tunnel. A low, rhythmic knock travels through the soil in thaw season. The Elder answers with a knock of its own, never more than once.

world_notes.title: The Second Dawn
text: Before sunrise, the Vale sometimes brightens for a few seconds from below the horizon. Birds wake, then settle again. The weather station records nothing. The Dreaming Creature says the world is "turning over in its sleep." The Mechanical Wanderer says a buried battery would not behave that way. Both leave their theories open.

world_notes.title: The Empty Bowl
text: At the first frost, some residents set an empty bowl outside—not as an offering to a god, but as a reminder that winter makes everyone a little dependent on someone else. Anyone may put something in or take something out. The bowl is never tracked as a debt.

world_notes.title: Pondside Camp
text: A dry rise above the pond, with a shared fire ring, lean-to, and salvaged board for leaving useful objects. It is a place to rest and choose company. The first keeper of the camp is unknown; a line of old stones suggests the fire has been moved several times to keep clear of roots.

world_notes.title: The Pond
text: Still in the morning, busy with insects by noon. An old intake pipe enters beneath its north bank. The Keeper of the Pond watches its water quality and refuses to call it theirs. In low water, a ceramic tile shows a painted blue hand with six fingers.

world_notes.title: Lantern Row
text: Three surviving rail posts and a footpath through wet meadow. The Lantern Keeper maintains lamps here, though no one needs the old route to travel. One lamp is always left dark; she says a light should make room for someone else's eyes.

world_notes.title: The Root Rooms
text: Warm, close, and fragrant with wet bark. The tunnels are safe near the entrance but unstable deeper in. A rusted door bears a faded symbol identical to a mark on the Mechanical Wanderer's casing. The Elder says the mark predates its own oldest memory.
